sites.loses: nothing observable: kimi-k3 is a Router catalog id, so this is a straight host unlock, not a lossy adaptation.
sites.why: Moonshot speaks the OpenAI wire format, so Router can serve it once its host is unlocked, per the task's guidance that another vendor's OpenAI-compatible endpoint can move when the model is in Router's catalog (kimi-k3 is). The CLI's `wrap`/`adapt --unlock-host` couldn't thread unlock_hosts through a LangChain ChatOpenAI wrapper (its `wrap_langchain` helper doesn't accept that option), and a `check --run` proved the CLI-only wrap left it un-routed (still hit api.moonshot.ai in the sandboxed run). So this was done by hand, calling router_runtime.wrap_openai(..., unlock_hosts=['api.moonshot.ai']) directly on every underlying openai.OpenAI client langchain-openai builds for this ChatOpenAI instance (it builds two -- root_client and a separate one behind the chat.completions resource -- both must be unlocked, mirroring router_runtime.wrap_langchain's own attribute traversal). Verified live with `check --run`: a valid /v1/responses request reached the Router simulator for model kimi-k3. The static `check --all` scanner now shows this site as 'stays' because it no longer recognizes the hand-written wrap pattern -- that is a scanner limitation, not an actual regression; the dynamic check is the ground truth here.

Bespoke HTTP contract (custom JSON request/response shape via plain `requests.post`, see hedge_fund/llm/contract.py), not an OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses or Anthropic Messages wire format. Router serves only /v1/responses, /v1/messages (+count_tokens) and /v1/models -- it has no endpoint that speaks TypeSafe's contract, so there is nothing to wrap, unlock, or adapt. This is the 'Router physically can't serve it' case.
